title: Part
spec: To construct the first part of the rectangular section, start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to -90.0, 0.0, -90.0 degrees and a translation vector of 0.0, 0.0, 0.0. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face, creating the first loop. This involves drawing four lines: the first line from the start point (0.0, 0.0) to the end point (0.0251, 0.0), the second line from (0.0251, 0.0) to (0.0251, 0.0753), the third line from (0.0251, 0.0753) to (0.0, 0.0753), and the fourth line from (0.0, 0.0753) back to (0.0, 0.0). Apply a sketch scale of 0.0753 to the two-dimensional sketch. Transform this scaled sketch into three-dimensional space by rotating it using the Euler angles -90.0, 0.0, -90.0 degrees and translating it with the vector 0.0, 0.0, 0.0. Extrude the sketch to create a three-dimensional model, setting the extrude depth towards the normal to 0.75 and the extrude depth opposite the normal to 0.0. The resulting shape will be a new solid body with a length of 0.02508361204013378, a width of 0.07525083612040134, and a height of 0.75. This completes the construction of the first part, which forms the rectangular section of the final cylindrical object.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch for the rectangular section
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0251, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0251, 0.0753) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0753) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create the rectangular section
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
# The translation vector is [0, 0, 0], so no translation is needed
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'
